scope: 4D's formula editor (EDIT FORMULA, and the Order By editor's Add Formula… and Modify…), published by the native plugin alone from its form's layers: the help line; the Tables, Operators and Commands menus as pop-up buttons; fields, operators and commands as buttons that insert them with a double click; tables and themes of commands as disclosure triangles read from the chevron 4D draws and pressed on it; the formula as an editable text field that is the focused element while it holds 4D's caret; and Load…, Save…, Cancel and OK; a formula built and written through accessibility and returned to the application, which evaluates it; by AX and by VoiceOver
fixture: prepare_formula_editor_fixture.py and test_formula_editor_fixture.py (Orders table with five records)
checks: the formula editor is pixel-identical to the plugin-free editor
the table's fields are buttons, after the menu that chooses the tables
the operators are buttons, after the menu that chooses their kind
the themes of commands are collapsed disclosure triangles
the formula is a text field holding the formula
Load, Save, Cancel and OK are buttons
writing the formula replaces it
pressing a field inserts it, as its double click does
pressing an operator inserts it
pressing a theme expands it, its commands following it
pressing it again collapses it
the commands menu lists the commands alphabetically, as buttons
pressing a command inserts it
the tables menu lists the tables, collapsed
pressing a table shows its fields
the formula is written as a keyboard user types it
OK returns the formula, which the application evaluates
VoiceOver reaches the formula editor
VoiceOver reads a theme of commands as collapsed
VO-Space on it expands it, showing its commands
VoiceOver reads the fields
VO-Space on a field inserts it into the formula
VoiceOver reads the formula as an edit field
typing replaces the formula, and VoiceOver echoes it
VoiceOver reaches OK
VO-Space on OK returns the formula, which the application evaluates
